_comment: Kid-safe educational topic seeds. Each entry produces a unique Short. Add more freely. The generator picks unused ones round-robin.

topics.hook: Octopuses have blue blood.
Honey never spoils.
Saturn would float.
topics.punchline: If you found a big enough ocean.

topics.hook: You replace your skin every month.
Lightning is hotter than the Sun.
Bananas are slightly radioactive.
A day on Venus is longer than its year.
A blue whale's tongue weighs as much as an elephant.
You can't see the Great Wall from space.
The shortest war lasted 38 minutes.
Hot water can freeze faster than cold.
Sloths take a month to digest one meal.
Every tongue print is unique.
Raindrops fall at 7 metres per second.
The Moon drifts 3.8cm away each year.
Wombat poo is cube-shaped.
An octave is double the frequency.
Git stores snapshots, not diffs.
Flexbox replaced 90% of CSS layout hacks.
Tab can navigate any web form.
Shift-click selects a range.
topics.punchline: Works in every list, every app.

topics.hook: Ctrl+F searches any page.
You cycle through 5 sleep stages.
Salt water is denser than fresh.
Bats see with sound.
Some years have a leap second.
Rainbows are full circles.
topics.punchline: We only see the top arc.

topics.hook: 9:16 fills the phone screen.
topics.punchline: That's why we built around it.

topics.hook: Five AIs answer one prompt.
MIT licence means take it and ship it.
Cats have 32 muscles in each ear.
Flamingos are born white.
Crows can remember human faces.
Elephants are the only mammals that cannot jump.
Male seahorses carry the babies.
Butterflies taste with their feet.
Jellyfish have no brain, heart, or blood.
Snails can sleep for 3 years straight.
Koalas have fingerprints nearly identical to humans.
Some parrots outlive their owners.
The platypus hunts by detecting electrical fields.
A year on Mercury is only 88 Earth days.
Jupiter has 95 known moons.
The Sun contains 99.8% of the solar system's mass.
Sound cannot travel through space.
More stars exist than grains of sand on Earth.
Mars has the tallest volcano in the solar system.
Neptune was discovered by mathematics, not a telescope.
Footprints on the Moon will last millions of years.
Earth spins at 1,670 km per hour at the equator.
Sunlight takes 8 minutes to reach Earth.
topics.punchline: You are always seeing the past.

topics.hook: Your body has more bacteria than human cells.
Trees share nutrients through underground fungal networks.
Your nose can detect over a trillion different smells.
A teaspoon of soil holds more organisms than all humans alive.
Humans emit faint visible light.
The human eye can detect a single photon of light.
Your body replaces most of its atoms every few years.
Water is the only substance that naturally exists in all three states on Earth.
The Eiffel Tower was built to be temporary.
Oxford University is older than the Aztec Empire.
Cleopatra lived closer to the Moon landing than to the pyramids.
Nintendo was founded in 1889.
The first vending machine was built in ancient Greece.
The first text message was sent in 1992.
topics.punchline: Typed on a computer, not a phone.

topics.hook: Vikings reached North America 500 years before Columbus.
Strawberries are not technically berries.
Carrots were originally purple.
Aztecs used chocolate as currency.
A child invented the popsicle by accident.
Bread has been baked for at least 14,000 years.
Beethoven was completely deaf when he wrote his Ninth Symphony.
A piano has exactly 88 keys.
The first computer bug was a real moth.
QWERTY was not designed for typing speed.
topics.punchline: It was built for telegraph operators.

topics.hook: Ctrl+Z undoes your last action in almost every app.
The @ symbol was used in accounting before email existed.
topics.punchline: It meant at a price of.

topics.hook: Copy and paste was invented by Larry Tesler in 1974.
topics.punchline: You use it every single day.

topics.hook: The spacebar is the most-pressed key on any keyboard.
topics.punchline: Used more than all letters combined.

topics.hook: The very first website is still online today.
Fog is just a cloud at ground level.
Thunder is the sound of air exploding around lightning.
A camel can drink 100 litres in ten minutes.
A peregrine falcon dives at 380 km per hour.
An ant can carry fifty times its own weight.
topics.punchline: Scaled up, that is a car.

topics.hook: Honeybees give directions by waggling.
Owl feathers break up air to silence flight.
A 2000 year old date seed was grown into a tree.
Saffron costs more per gram than gold.
Some olive trees still fruit after 2000 years.
Lightning striking sand creates glass tubes.
A thin film of water turns salt flats into a mirror.
Fold paper 42 times and it reaches the Moon.
Old window glass is not slowly flowing.
The numerals you use every day came through Arabic.
Baghdad had a library that translated the known world.
Algebra is named after an Arabic word.
The astrolabe could find your latitude from a star.
Paper reached Europe through Samarkand.
Coffee drinking began in Yemen.
Ctrl+Shift+T reopens the tab you just closed.
Shift+F3 changes text case in most editors.
Screen readers rely on correct HTML headings.
Naming things and cache invalidation are the two hard problems.
Binary search finds one item in a million in twenty steps.
The first video game was built on an oscilloscope.
The Konami code was a debug shortcut.
topics.punchline: A developer could not finish his own game.

topics.hook: Playing Tetris can change how you dream.
topics.punchline: Researchers named it the Tetris effect.

topics.hook: A pixel is short for picture element.
Speedrun records are decided by single frames.
Every game runs the same three steps forever.
60fps means the screen redraws every 16 milliseconds.
topics.punchline: Miss it and the eye notices.

topics.hook: Some games generate their worlds from a single number.
Game characters are mostly invisible boxes.
topics.punchline: You collide with the box, not the art.

topics.hook: A neural network is layers of simple sums.
topics.punchline: Depth is where the power comes from.

topics.hook: AI models read tokens, not words.
topics.punchline: One word can be several tokens.

topics.hook: Training a model and using it are different jobs.
topics.punchline: One takes months, one takes milliseconds.

topics.hook: A GPU does thousands of small sums at once.
topics.punchline: That is why it trains models.

topics.hook: A context window is how much a model can hold at once.
topics.punchline: Beyond it, earlier text falls away.

topics.hook: AI turns words into coordinates.
AI upscaling invents pixels that were never captured.
Game characters navigate using A star.
topics.punchline: Guess the distance, take the best guess.

topics.hook: Computer randomness is not actually random.
topics.punchline: It is a formula with a starting number.
